root_cause.text: ksmbd validated SMB2/SMB3 request signatures and NTLMv2 MACs with `memcmp()` in `fs/smb/server/auth.c` and `fs/smb/server/smb2pdu.c`, making the comparison early-exit and therefore timing-dependent instead of constant-time.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `memcmp(ntlmv2->ntlmv2_hash, ntlmv2_rsp, ...)` and both `memcmp(signature, signature_req, SMB2_SIGNATURE_SIZE)` checks with `crypto_memneq()`, and the commit message explicitly says this is “To prevent timing attacks, MAC comparisons need to be constant-time.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the missing crypto utility dependency to SMB_SERVER so its crypto features can build and run correctly.
intent_record.what: In the SMB_SERVER Kconfig section, a new dependency line was added: `select CRYPTO_LIB_UTILS`.
intent_record.how: Building or enabling SMB_SERVER will now also pull in the crypto utility library support it depends on, ensuring the required crypto helper functions are available at runtime and link time.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the crypto utils header so the file can use crypto utility helpers.
intent_record.what: A new header include, <crypto/utils.h>, was added alongside the existing crypto and Linux includes.
intent_record.how: This makes declarations or inline helpers from the crypto utilities header available to the file, enabling use of those crypto utility APIs during compilation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace a non-constant-time NTLMv2 hash comparison with a constant-time crypto-safe check in ksmbd_auth_ntlmv2().
intent_record.what: In ksmbd_auth_ntlmv2(), the byte-for-byte comparison of ntlmv2->ntlmv2_hash and ntlmv2_rsp was changed from memcmp() to crypto_memneq(), with the same hash-length argument retained.
intent_record.how: Runtime behavior for this check remains a mismatch test, but it now uses the kernel’s constant-time comparison helper instead of a potentially timing-variable memcmp(), reducing the chance of leaking information through comparison timing while still returning -EINVAL on mismatch.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the missing crypto utils header so the file can compile and use required crypto helper definitions.
intent_record.what: The diff adds a single include directive: `#include <crypto/utils.h>` at the top of the file, above the existing Linux networking headers.
intent_record.how: This change makes declarations or inline helpers from `crypto/utils.h` available to the translation unit, allowing the code in this file to use crypto utility functions or types without implicit declarations or build failures.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace the SMB2 signature comparison with a constant-time crypto-safe equality check.
intent_record.what: The code in `smb2_check_sign_req()` changed the signature comparison from `memcmp(signature, signature_req, SMB2_SIGNATURE_SIZE)` to `crypto_memneq(signature, signature_req, SMB2_SIGNATURE_SIZE)`.
intent_record.how: Runtime behavior remains a signature-equality check, but it now uses a cryptographically suitable constant-time comparison helper instead of a standard byte-wise compare, reducing the risk of timing-based information leakage during SMB2 signature verification.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use a constant-time comparison for SMB3 signature verification to avoid timing side-channel leakage.
intent_record.what: The code replaces a `memcmp(signature, signature_req, SMB2_SIGNATURE_SIZE)` comparison with `crypto_memneq(signature, signature_req, SMB2_SIGNATURE_SIZE)` in `smb3_check_sign_req()`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the signature verification now uses a constant-time memory comparison helper instead of a standard byte comparison, reducing the risk of timing-based information leakage while preserving the same equality check behavior.

consistency_review.core_intent: Replace SMB-related authentication/signature comparisons with constant-time checks to prevent timing side-channel leakage.

relevance_review.reason: The change only adds a missing crypto utility dependency for SMB_SERVER build/runtime support. It does not modify the signature/MAC comparison logic in auth.c or smb2pdu.c, nor does it address the timing-dependent memcmp() vulnerability.
The change only adds a crypto utilities header and does not address the vulnerable use of memcmp() for SMB signature/NTLMv2 MAC verification or make the comparison constant-time.
The changes directly address the root cause by replacing memcmp-based SMB2/SMB3 signature and NTLMv2 MAC comparisons with constant-time checks in the same ksmbd authentication paths.

The change only adds a missing crypto utils header for compilation; it does not modify the signature/MAC comparison logic or replace memcmp() with a constant-time comparison, so it is unrelated to the timing vulnerability.

candidates.rationale: This pre-fix memcmp() performs the NTLMv2 MAC/hash verification in a timing-dependent, early-exit manner, which matches the root cause.
This pre-fix memcmp() checks the SMB2 signature non-constantly, leaking timing differences based on matching prefix length.
This pre-fix memcmp() verifies the SMB3 signature in a timing-dependent way, directly embodying the vulnerability.

vuln_statements.explanation: This NTLMv2 MAC/hash verification uses memcmp(), which can exit early on the first differing byte and therefore leaks timing information instead of performing a constant-time comparison.
This SMB2/SMB3 signature check uses memcmp(), making signature verification timing-dependent and vulnerable to side-channel leakage based on matched prefix length.
